title: Road Trips from Hyderabad: Heritage, Forests and Long Drives
seoTitle: Road Trips from Hyderabad: Heritage, Forests, Rivers
metaDescription: Road trips from Hyderabad: Ananthagiri, Warangal and Ramappa, Nagarjuna Sagar, Srisailam, Bidar, Laknavaram, Bhadrachalam, Hampi, Gandikota and Goa.
description: A guide to road trips from Hyderabad: short drives to Ananthagiri Hills, Pochampally and Bidar, weekend trips to Warangal and Ramappa, Nagarjuna Sagar, Srisailam through the Nallamala forest, Laknavaram and Bhadrachalam, and longer drives to Hampi, Gandikota and the Belum caves, and Goa, with approximate distances, the Amrabad forest night closure and seasons.
dek: From Hyderabad, road trips lead to Kakatiya temples, Deccan forts, Krishna river gorges and, further afield, Hampi and Goa.

hero.alt: The Nallamala hills on the road to Srisailam

intro: Hyderabad sits on the Deccan plateau, and its road trips reflect that landscape: rocky hills, reservoirs and forests, with dynastic capitals scattered across them. To the north-east lie Warangal and the UNESCO-listed Ramappa temple; to the south, the Nallamala forest and the Krishna gorge at Srisailam; to the west, Bidar's fort; and further south-west, Hampi and Gandikota.
Most roads are good highways, but forest roads through the Amrabad Tiger Reserve close at night.
quickAnswer: The best road trips from Hyderabad are Ananthagiri Hills (about 80 km), Pochampally (about 50 km), Bidar (about 145 km), Warangal and Ramappa (about 150 to 210 km), Nagarjuna Sagar (about 160 km), Srisailam (about 215 km, through the Nallamala forest), Laknavaram (about 220 km), Bhadrachalam (about 310 km), Hampi (about 375 km) and Goa (about 650 km). October to February is best; the monsoon greens the forests.
takeaways: Warangal and Ramappa make an excellent heritage weekend.
The road to Srisailam crosses the Amrabad Tiger Reserve, which closes at night.
Ananthagiri Hills is the nearest green escape.
Hampi and Gandikota are long drives, best as three- to four-day trips.
Summer (April to June) is very hot on the Deccan.

sections.heading: Road trips from Hyderabad at a glance

items.name: Warangal and Ramappa
body: The Kakatiya fort, the Thousand Pillar temple and the UNESCO-listed Ramappa temple.

items.name: Bidar
body: A Bahmani fort and tombs, west of Hyderabad.

items.name: Hampi
body: The Vijayanagara capital, a long but rewarding drive.

items.name: Srisailam
body: Through the Nallamala hills and the Amrabad Tiger Reserve to the Krishna gorge and the Mallikarjuna temple.

items.name: Nagarjuna Sagar
body: A great masonry dam and an island museum of Buddhist relics.

items.name: Ananthagiri and Laknavaram
body: A forested hill near the city, and a lake with a hanging bridge.

items.name: Bhadrachalam and the Godavari
body: A temple town and boat trips into the Papikondalu gorge.

sections.heading: Forest night closure
paras: The road to Srisailam passes through the Amrabad Tiger Reserve, where traffic is usually stopped at night, roughly between 9 pm and 6 am. Plan to cross in daylight, keep to the speed limit and do not stop in the forest.

items.name: Gandikota, Belum and Goa
body: Gandikota's gorge and the Belum caves in Andhra, or the long drive west to Goa.

sections.heading: Tips for driving out of Hyderabad
list: The Outer Ring Road makes it easy to exit the city in any direction; leave early.
Carry water and avoid midday walking at sites in summer.
Srisailam is busy with pilgrims on festival days, especially Maha Shivaratri.
Check whether the Papikondalu boat services are running before driving to Bhadrachalam.

sections.heading: Planning a long weekend
paras: With three days, pair Warangal and Ramappa with Laknavaram lake, or Nagarjuna Sagar with Srisailam through the Nallamala forest. With four or five days, drive to Hampi via Raichur or Kurnool, returning via Gandikota and the Belum caves. On the road, stop for Hyderabadi biryani before you leave and try Warangal's local sweets.

sections.heading: When to go
paras: October to February is best, with pleasant days on the Deccan. The monsoon (June to September) turns the forests green and fills the reservoirs, making Nagarjuna Sagar and Srisailam dramatic when the dam gates open. April to June is very hot.

safety: Mountain roads close or slow down after heavy rain, snow or landslides; check road status and weather updates each morning and avoid driving after dark.
Permits, tolls, entry fees, pass openings and road works change; check official sources shortly before you travel.
Distances and driving times are approximate and vary with traffic, weather, road works and stops.
packing: Driving licence, RC, insurance and PUC certificate, with copies
Warm layers and a rain jacket
Cash for small towns and barriers

faqs.q: What are the best weekend road trips from Hyderabad?
faqs.a: Warangal and Ramappa, Nagarjuna Sagar, Srisailam, Ananthagiri Hills and Bidar.

faqs.q: Is the Srisailam road open at night?
faqs.a: The forest stretch through the Amrabad Tiger Reserve usually closes at night; plan to cross in daylight.

faqs.q: How far is Hampi from Hyderabad?
faqs.a: About 375 km, usually around seven hours.

faqs.q: What is the nearest hill getaway to Hyderabad?
faqs.a: Ananthagiri Hills, about two hours away.
